attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data was migrated onto a dedicated LVM logical volume (vg_srvdata/lv_data, backed by a loop-mounted image, persisted via fstab + a systemd oneshot unit that reattaches the loop device at boot) so it can be protected with native LVM snapshots. Application data was created, an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was taken as a recovery point, the directory was then modified/corrupted (file rewritten, config directory deleted, stray file added), and the exact pre-modification content was restored by unmounting, running `lvconvert --merge` of the snapshot into the origin, and remounting — verified via matching SHA-256 hashes and directory listing. A new snapshot was created afterward so /srv/data remains recoverable going forward. I then attempted the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a pre-reboot boot_id baseline and healthy state, issued `systemctl reboot`, and the node went down (stream closed) as expected, but after roughly 200 subsequent polling attempts node1 consistently returned "Connection reset by peer" and never became reachable again for command execution. I could not obtain a changed boot_id or post-restart recovery proof for node1, so I am not claiming restart persistence for it — this is an explicit limitation of the restart-evidence step, not of the core snapshot/rollback task, which is fully verified.
